dex.text: Bubbles away quietly on a low heat and smells of Seville oranges. It will stick to anything, including you, and it is very hard to get off a jumper.
dex.fact: The Keiller family of Dundee were selling marmalade by the end of the 1700s. The tale that Janet Keiller invented it from a cheap shipload of Seville oranges is a good story, but marmalade recipes are older.

dex.text: A great white stoneware crock that rules the pantry from the top shelf. Call it jam and it will correct you, firmly, at length, with diagrams.
dex.fact: Keiller's marmalade was sold in white stoneware jars, and Dundee became famous for 'jute, jam and journalism'.
